title: This Java Class Won't Let You Cancel Twice
description:
Inside the Java Mastery Path capstone — a real Order Management REST API — the Order entity itself blocks a double-cancel, and a global exception handler turns that violation into the exact HTTP status a REST client expects. It's layered architecture in miniature: domain guards, service translation, and a global handler, each doing one job.

Source lesson:
- https://sigilipelli.github.io/java-mastery-path/level-4/10-capstone-project/

#Shorts

beats.narration: In this capstone Order Management API, you literally cannot cancel the same order twice. Here's the tiny bit of Java that enforces it.

display.heading: Cancel Twice? Not So Fast.
display.subheading: Java Mastery Path — Level 4 Capstone: Order Management Service

beats.narration: The order entity guards its own state. Cancel it once, fine. Try again, and it throws, right there in the domain model, no controller code needed.
The service layer catches that exception and turns it into a typed one — InvalidOrderStateException — instead of leaking a generic runtime error up to the API.
And this global handler maps it straight to an HTTP 409 Conflict — the exact status code REST clients expect when they retry a bad action.
That's the whole capstone in miniature: domain logic, a service layer, and a global handler, each doing exactly one job.

display.heading: One state check, three layers deep
display.subheading: Layered architecture, validated input, global error handling — the same shape as real production Java services
